title: Network Volume Terms for Summit Gold Status Awards under Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements
content:
**Terms.** The Gold network percentage of a Summit Gold status award redeemed from Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements company points is set by two network measures of the company, both taken in the Gold network window of 12 calendar months up to and including the redemption date, from the fare ledger of the company's tickets under Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand:

- the fares collected on invoice on the company's tickets, placed by collection date — the fare collections paid by corporate invoice;
- the flown coupons on the company's tickets, placed by flight date.

The Gold network percentage is 85 percent when those invoiced fares reach USD 90000 and those flown coupons reach 24 together; it is 92 percent when the fares reach USD 45000 and the coupons reach 12 together, without both of the first pair of conditions being met; and it is 100 percent, the full price, in every other case.

| Invoiced fares in the window | Flown coupons in the window | Gold network percentage |
|---|---|---|
| USD 90000 or more | 24 or more | 85 |
| USD 90000 or more | 12 to 23 | 92 |
| USD 45000 to below 90000 | 12 or more | 92 |
| USD 45000 or more | fewer than 12 | 100 |
| below USD 45000 | any number | 100 |

**How the percentage acts.** The Gold network percentage multiplies the standard Gold award price, the tier's Summit Gold status-award points. Where the price carries several such percentages, they are all applied together to the standard price, each divided by one hundred, and the product is rounded to the nearest whole point once.

### Cases (hypothetical)

- Invoiced fares of USD 95000.00 with 20 flown coupons: the coupon condition of the 85 percent row fails, both conditions of the 92 percent row hold, so 92 percent.
- Invoiced fares of USD 44000.00 with 40 flown coupons: neither pair holds, so 100 percent.
- Fares paid by card do not count as invoiced fares, however many coupons are flown.
